candidate_datasets.role: human embryonic and fetal developmental material and data

obstacles: Pregnancy age may be counted from conception or last menstrual period.
Embryonic sex and exact age are not known for every specimen.
'Ant-sized' is an imprecise comparison.
rationale: Human embryo collections and reconstructions directly document size and organ visibility by stage. Sex-specific genital visibility at the stated age is especially discriminating, though dating conventions require care.

operationalization: Compare sex-specific fetal anatomical milestones and gestational-age-at-birth distributions in large ultrasound and birth cohorts.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: large public birth microdata with infant sex and gestational age

candidate_datasets.name: NICHD Fetal Growth Studies
candidate_datasets.role: longitudinal ultrasound measures of fetal development

obstacles: 'Completes its parts' needs specified developmental milestones.
Ancient ten-month dating differs from modern gestational weeks.
rationale: Sex, gestational duration and repeated fetal measurements exist in large contemporary datasets. A milestone definition is needed, but the predicted sex differences are readily and powerfully testable.

operationalization: Compare within-species gestation-length distributions across humans and other mammals and test whether nonhuman species have zero variation and humans uniquely span the stated months.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: human gestational-age distributions

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: mammalian gestation traits

obstacles: Species databases often report a range or mean rather than individual gestations.
Ancient month counting is ambiguous.
Comparing all animals is taxonomically vast.
rationale: Human variation is documented in millions of births, and individual variation in other mammals is available in breeding and veterinary data. The uniqueness and fixed-term assertions are strong enough for existing counterexamples to resolve.

operationalization: Estimate survival to discharge and later ages by gestational week, focusing on births before twenty-eight weeks and comparing with seven-month births.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: public linked birth and infant-death data by gestational age

candidate_datasets.name: Vermont Oxford Network
candidate_datasets.role: neonatal outcomes resources for very preterm infants

obstacles: Modern neonatal intensive care differs radically from ancient conditions.
Month-to-week conversion is approximate.
rationale: Gestational age and survival are available in very large public vital-statistics data. The absolute 'never' claim is decisively testable today, although historical viability under ancient care is a different question.

operationalization: Compare neonatal survival for approximately thirty-two-week births in Egypt and Greece, standardized by birth year, birth weight, plurality and level of care.

candidate_datasets.name: WHO Global Health Observatory
candidate_datasets.role: country-level maternal and neonatal health indicators

candidate_datasets.name: Eurostat
candidate_datasets.role: European birth and mortality statistics including Greece

obstacles: Public microdata with exact gestational age are uneven across both countries.
Modern care strongly confounds geography.
The claim may concern ancient rather than current populations.
rationale: Contemporary national and international neonatal data can test the geographic survival contrast, at least in aggregate. They cannot cleanly reconstruct ancient Egyptian and Greek outcomes, so temporal interpretation materially affects the result.

operationalization: Find the maximum plurality among documented human deliveries in vital records and verify births above five with clinical records.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: public birth data including plurality

candidate_datasets.name: Human Multiple Births Database
candidate_datasets.role: international multiple-birth statistics

obstacles: Extreme historical cases require verification of live versus still births.
Some public files top-code very high plurality.
rationale: Plurality is routinely recorded in large birth registries, making the maximum claim directly testable. Verified sextuplet and higher-order deliveries can serve as decisive counterexamples without estimating a population rate.

operationalization: Define acceptance as observed receptive mating behavior and compare its rate during pregnancy among women, mares, hares and representative other mammals.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open animal behavioral and reproduction study datasets

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative reproductive-behavior literature

obstacles: Human sexual behavior is not directly comparable to animal estrus.
Pregnancy-stage mating behavior is not broadly standardized.
The superlative 'most inclined' requires exhaustive coverage.
rationale: The claim can be operationalized behaviorally, but comparable cross-species data are sparse and conceptually heterogeneous. Existing studies can test individual taxa and exceptions, not the full ranking.

operationalization: Estimate age distributions for natural menopause and childbirth, testing modal cessation near forty, an upper limit near fifty and absence of births beyond fifty.

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international birth histories and menopause-related survey measures

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: maternal age in public birth records

obstacles: Assisted reproduction complicates the relation between menopause and childbirth.
Survey-defined menopause can be affected by surgery or contraception.
rationale: Menopause and maternal age are standard variables in large public datasets. The age distribution and claimed hard upper bound can both be tested directly, with sensitivity analyses for assisted conception.

operationalization: Estimate paternity and birth counts by paternal age, testing continued fatherhood through ages sixty and seventy while distinguishing sexual function from proven fertility.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: public birth records containing paternal age

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international male fertility and birth-history data

obstacles: Paternity at a given age does not measure general sexual competence.
Paternal age is missing from some birth records.
rationale: Large birth datasets readily establish whether men father children at sixty and seventy and estimate frequency. The broader sexual-competence component requires survey or clinical proxies but is also widely measured.

operationalization: Separate inherited genetic disorders from acquired scars, then compare parent-child concordance using pedigrees, diagnoses and image-derived marks.

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man
candidate_datasets.role: curated human inherited phenotypes and genetic disorders

candidate_datasets.name: dbGaP
candidate_datasets.role: genotype-phenotype family studies, many requiring controlled access

obstacles: Lameness and blindness have both inherited and acquired causes.
Scars are acquired and are not coded in most pedigrees.
Many family datasets are controlled rather than openly downloadable.
rationale: Heritable deformities are strongly testable with established pedigree and genetic resources. The assertion that acquired marks such as scars are transmitted needs rare linked observations and is not supported by a broad public dataset.

operationalization: Quantify facial or trait resemblance across three-generation pedigrees and test whether grandchildren can resemble grandparents more than their intervening parent.

candidate_datasets.name: dbGaP
candidate_datasets.role: multigenerational genotype-phenotype studies

candidate_datasets.name: Open Humans
candidate_datasets.role: participant-contributed public personal and genomic data

obstacles: Resemblance requires specified traits or image metrics.
Multigenerational identifiable images are privacy-sensitive.
Most dbGaP individual data require authorization.
rationale: Mendelian segregation and multigenerational phenotype data make skipped resemblance directly testable for defined traits. Privacy limits some access, but existing data and standard genetic methods are sufficient for resolution.

operationalization: Define comparable embryonic processes and attachment structures, then map yolk-sac, placenta and umbilical or vitelline connections across representative animal phyla.

candidate_datasets.name: Bgee
candidate_datasets.role: comparative developmental anatomy and expression across species

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon
candidate_datasets.role: cross-species anatomy ontology for homologous developmental structures

obstacles: 'Develop in the same way' is too broad without chosen homologous stages.
Many animals lack a navel-like structure.
Coverage across all animal phyla is uneven.
rationale: Attachment structures can be compared using anatomy ontologies and developmental data, and counterexamples are accessible. The overarching sameness claim is underspecified and cannot be resolved as a single proposition.

operationalization: Compile fetal presentation near term and presentation at delivery across viviparous species, testing the universal head-first assertion and the claimed prenatal turn.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: human birth presentation and delivery records

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central
candidate_datasets.role: open veterinary obstetric studies across mammals

obstacles: Presentation terminology differs across taxa.
Broad individual-level veterinary data are scattered.
Tail-first delivery may be normal in some species.
rationale: Birth presentation is routinely recorded in humans and veterinary medicine. The universal wording is decisively testable with documented normal posterior presentations even without complete coverage of every viviparous animal.

operationalization: Count arteries and veins in umbilical or yolk-sac connections from cattle, smaller mammals and chicken embryos, then test whether vessel number follows body size.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anatomical imaging across vertebrates

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public embryo imaging datasets

obstacles: Bird yolk-sac vessels are not anatomically identical to a mammalian umbilical cord.
Vessel count changes across developmental stages.
Size categories are vague.
rationale: Vessel number is direct and visible in existing embryological images and anatomical literature. Homology and stage must be standardized, but the numeric size rule can be clearly confirmed or refuted.

operationalization: Estimate age and order of primary-tooth eruption from pediatric cohorts, then test any association with measured breast-milk temperature.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
candidate_datasets.role: public dental examination and age data

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international child health and feeding data

obstacles: Milk temperature is rarely measured and 'warmer' may be metaphorical.
Cross-sectional dental exams interval-censor eruption age.
rationale: Timing and order of tooth eruption are well covered in public pediatric data and resolve the main claim. The milk-temperature mechanism lacks a standard variable and is only weakly assessable from existing resources.

operationalization: Estimate menstrual resumption as a function of exclusive and partial breastfeeding duration, while testing the proposed general suppression and documented exceptions.

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international breastfeeding, postpartum amenorrhea and birth-history data

obstacles: Lactation intensity and supplementation strongly affect amenorrhea.
The moisture-allocation explanation is not directly represented in surveys.
rationale: Breastfeeding and postpartum amenorrhea are jointly measured in large public surveys, providing a direct test of the generalization and exceptions. The physiological explanation requires separate endocrine evidence but has measurable alternatives.

operationalization: Define behavioral measures for fear, aggression, affiliative behavior and problem solving, then estimate their presence and cross-species continuity across sampled animals and humans.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal QTLdb
candidate_datasets.role: public behavioral trait records for domesticated animals

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative animal cognition and behavior datasets

obstacles: Psychical qualities are anthropomorphic and multidimensional.
'Traces' makes nearly any behavior compatible.
Most animals have never been tested comparably.
rationale: Individual capacities can be operationalized with modern behavioral assays, but the very broad analogical claim has weak falsification criteria. Existing data can resolve selected qualities and taxa only.

operationalization: No unique dataset analysis can decide whether a chosen living/nonliving boundary is 'sharp'; trait matrices could only display gradients under a prespecified philosophical definition.
obstacles: Life and animal boundaries are classification choices.
Intermediate morphology does not by itself make a boundary impossible.
The proposed gradual order lacks a defined metric.
rationale: Data can document mixtures of traits in sponges, ascidians and other organisms, but every pattern remains compatible with multiple definitions of life and animality. The claim's central conclusion is conceptual rather than a discriminating empirical prediction.

operationalization: Relate standardized cognition or memory scores to duration of postnatal association and frequency of social interaction across species, controlling lifespan and developmental mode.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative cognition and parental-care datasets

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: developmental and reproductive covariates across vertebrates

obstacles: Comparable intelligence scores are unavailable for most taxa.
Parental association reflects ecology and development as well as cognition.
Memory and sociality are distinct constructs.
rationale: Parental-care duration is measurable, and selected comparative cognition datasets allow a restricted correlation test. Coverage and confounding are too severe for the general causal ranking.

operationalization: For each named taxon, verify respiratory organs, surfacing intervals, response to prevented air access, and breeding habitat.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public species accounts for respiration and reproduction

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: movement and dive records for aquatic air-breathing animals

obstacles: Frogs and some turtles can exchange gases through skin or cloaca.
Breeding habitat varies among species within the named groups.
rationale: Respiration, surfacing and breeding habitats are standard natural-history variables with broad public documentation. The compound universal is resolvable, including clear exceptions to simplified drowning or land-breeding language.

operationalization: Combine cetacean anatomy, dive records, bycatch mortality and sleep observations to test lung breathing, suffocation in nets, out-of-water survival and breathing during rest.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: cetacean movement and dive studies

candidate_datasets.name: OBIS-SEAMAP
candidate_datasets.role: public marine megavertebrate observations and survey data

obstacles: Out-of-water survival depends on species and conditions.
Sleep posture is difficult to observe in wild dolphins.
Bycatch records may not distinguish cause of death.
rationale: The respiratory anatomy and need to surface are directly established, while tracking and bycatch data address behavior and suffocation. Some duration and sleep details are less comprehensively sampled but remain testable.

operationalization: Measure water flow, oxygen uptake and heat exchange across fish gills, and separately test whether cetacean blowholes admit water during prey capture.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish respiratory physiology and ecology

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central
candidate_datasets.role: open gill physiology and cetacean respiratory anatomy studies

obstacles: Cooling and oxygen uptake occur simultaneously and need causal separation.
The claim incorrectly groups gills and blowholes under water intake.
Physiological datasets are species-specific.
rationale: Existing physiology can distinguish respiratory gas exchange from thermoregulation and test blowhole anatomy. The broad proposed common purpose is only partially comparable across the two very different systems.

operationalization: Map cordylus to candidate salamanders and compare adult respiratory organs, limb-supported terrestrial locomotion and feeding habitat.

candidate_datasets.name: AmphibiaWeb
candidate_datasets.role: public amphibian species accounts, life histories and morphology

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: occurrence records for candidate newt and salamander taxa

obstacles: The ancient animal may be a larva, neotenic adult or different amphibian.
Gill retention and terrestrial activity vary by life stage.
The uniqueness claim requires exhaustive animal coverage.
rationale: Candidate taxa have documented respiratory anatomy and habitat use, enabling tests under each mapping. Identity uncertainty and the 'only known animal' superlative prevent a single definitive assessment.

operationalization: Quantify phenotypic changes after castration and relate experimentally measured embryonic gonadal or sex-determining changes to later sexual phenotype.

candidate_datasets.name: Mouse Genome Informatics
candidate_datasets.role: public mouse genotype and developmental phenotype data

candidate_datasets.name: Animal QTLdb
candidate_datasets.role: livestock traits including reproductive and castration-associated phenotypes

obstacles: 'Minute organ' and 'female form' are vague.
Castration effects and embryonic sex determination are distinct mechanisms.
A slight organ-size change is not a general sex-determination rule.
rationale: Existing veterinary and model-organism data can quantify many castration and sex-development effects. The broad principle and the proposed organ-size decision mechanism require substantial interpretation and cannot be tested as one coherent causal claim.

operationalization: Submerge sealed, weighed thin wax vessels in seawater for twenty-four hours and assay recovered internal water volume and salinity against controls.
obstacles: No known public dataset records this exact experiment.
Vessel sealing, wax permeability and contamination must be controlled.
Running the simple experiment would constitute new data collection.
rationale: The prediction is exceptionally clear and a standard salinity assay would decide it. However, the task concerns existing datasets, and none is known to contain replicated measurements of this exact wax-vessel setup.

operationalization: Compile diet and stomach-content records for fishes, coding conspecific predation and testing both its universality and absence in Mugilidae.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish diet, food items and ecology records

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: public species-interaction records including predation

obstacles: Absence of recorded cannibalism is not proof of absence.
Diet sampling is sparse for many fishes.
Life-stage cannibalism may be underidentified.
rationale: The universal assertion can be refuted by well-sampled species lacking cannibalism or by documented mullet cannibalism. Existing diet and interaction resources support these tests, though not an exhaustive proof of absence for every fish.

operationalization: Inspect comparative fish anatomy for an esophagus between pharynx and stomach and distinguish true stomach eversion from regurgitation during prey capture.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public three-dimensional fish anatomical specimens

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish morphology and feeding biology

obstacles: Digestive anatomy varies greatly among fishes.
Some fishes lack a differentiated stomach but still have an esophagus.
rationale: The presence and position of an esophagus are directly visible in extensive comparative anatomy. Existing specimens and literature also separate stomach eversion from ordinary regurgitation, making the universal claim decisively testable.
